signals.reason: Close above CPR top 1445.42 (narrow CPR: trend day likely)
signals.rules: Close above the top central pivot (TC) = bullish bias; below the bottom central (BC) = bearish; inside the range = no bias. A narrow CPR (< 1/12 of the previous session's range) signals a trend day and strengthens the call.

signals.name: Camarilla Pivots

signals.name: VWAP Bands

signals.name: Opening Gap

signals.reason: Gap up +0.47% holding above the open (gap-and-go)

signals.name: Market Profile Value Area

signals.rules: Close above the value area high (VAH) = buyers accepting higher prices; below the value area low (VAL) = sellers in control; inside value = balance, lean by side of the point of control (POC).

signals.name: Williams Alligator
signals.origin: Bill Williams, 'Trading Chaos' (1995); SMMA 13/8/5 shifted 8/5/3
signals.rules: Lips above teeth above jaw with price above the lips = uptrend (long). The mirror = downtrend (short). Lines intertwined = the alligator sleeps: no trade.

signals.name: Golden / Death Cross

signals.reason: Price and moving averages not aligned
signals.rules: Bullish when SMA50 > SMA200 and price above both; bearish when SMA50 < SMA200 and price below.

signals.name: EMA 9/21 Crossover
signals.origin: Common swing-trading fast/slow EMA system

signals.name: MACD Crossover

signals.reason: MACD below signal; below zero line; histogram falling
signals.rules: Bullish: MACD above signal (esp. above zero) with rising histogram. Bearish: the reverse.

signals.name: ADX / DMI Trend
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978), 14-period
signals.rules: ADX > 25 = trending. +DI > -DI bullish, -DI > +DI bearish. ADX < 20 = no trend (neutral).

signals.name: Supertrend
signals.origin: Olivier Seban; ATR(10) x 3
signals.rules: Long while close is above the Supertrend line; short while below. Flips on close crossing the line.

signals.name: Parabolic SAR

signals.rules: Dots below price = uptrend (long); dots above price = downtrend (short).

signals.name: Ichimoku Cloud

signals.reason: price below cloud, Tenkan < Kijun, bearish (red) cloud, Chikou below price
signals.rules: Bullish: price above cloud, Tenkan > Kijun, green cloud (A > B). Bearish: the mirror. Inside cloud = neutral.

signals.name: Hull MA Slope

signals.rules: Long when HMA is rising and price above it; short when falling and price below.

signals.name: Elder Triple Screen
signals.origin: Dr. Alexander Elder, 'Trading for a Living' (1993)
signals.reason: Weekly-equivalent tide down (EMA13 falling, MACD-hist falling); Stoch 5

signals.rules: Stay long while close > 22-bar high - 3 ATR; stay short while close < 22-bar low + 3 ATR.

signals.name: Heikin-Ashi Trend
signals.origin: Japanese 'average bar' charting; widely used trend filter
signals.reason: 6 consecutive red HA candles with no opposing wick (strong)

signals.name: RSI 14 (Wilder)
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978)
signals.rules: RSI < 30 oversold (bullish reversal), > 70 overbought (bearish). Between: RSI > 50 bullish bias, < 50 bearish. Divergence strengthens the call.

signals.name: CCI (Lambert)

signals.name: Williams %R

signals.rules: OBV above its 20-EMA and rising confirms an uptrend (volume flows in); OBV falling while price rises = bearish divergence.

signals.name: VWAP
signals.origin: Institutional execution benchmark; standard intraday bias tool
signals.rules: Price above VWAP = bullish bias (longs favoured, VWAP acts as support); below = bearish. Distance is normalised by ATR.

signals.name: Money Flow Index
signals.origin: Gene Quong & Avrum Soudack; 14-period
signals.rules: MFI < 20 oversold (bullish), > 80 overbought (bearish).

signals.name: Chaikin Money Flow
signals.origin: Marc Chaikin; 20-period
signals.rules: CMF > +0.05 = buying pressure (bullish); < -0.05 = selling pressure (bearish).

signals.name: Candlestick Patterns
signals.origin: Steve Nison, 'Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques' (1991)
signals.reason: No notable pattern on the last bars
signals.rules: Detects Engulfing, Hammer / Hanging Man, Shooting Star, Morning / Evening Star, Three White Soldiers / Black Crows, Doji. Reversal patterns count more after an extended move.

signals.name: Pivot Points
signals.origin: Classic floor-trader pivots (CME pit tradition); previous session's H/L/C on intraday charts
signals.reason: Price at support S1 - bounce zone
signals.rules: Above the pivot = bullish bias, targets R1/R2; below = bearish, targets S1/S2. Price sitting at S1/R1 within 0.3 ATR is a bounce zone.

signals.name: Fibonacci Retracement
signals.origin: Classic Fibonacci pullback trading (Elliott / Gann tradition)
signals.reason: Down-swing intact, not at a fib level
signals.rules: In an up-swing, a pullback holding 38.2/50/61.8% is a buy zone; in a down-swing a bounce into those levels is a sell zone. Beyond 78.6% the swing is invalidated.

signals.name: Support / Resistance
signals.origin: Classic technical analysis (Edwards & Magee, 'Technical Analysis of Stock Trends', 1948)
signals.rules: Nearest swing-high resistance / swing-low support. A close through a level on the last bar = breakout; a hold within 0.5 ATR = bounce.

signals.name: Central Pivot Range (CPR)
signals.origin: Frank Ochoa, 'Secrets of a Pivot Boss' (2010); previous-session pivot, BC, TC
signals.rules: Close above the top central pivot (TC) = bullish bias; below the bottom central (BC) = bearish; inside the range = no bias. A narrow CPR (< 1/12 of the previous session's range) signals a trend day and strengthens the call.

signals.name: Camarilla Pivots
signals.origin: Nick Scott (1989); widely used by Indian intraday traders. H3/L3 reversal, H4/L4 breakout
signals.reason: At L3 1191.36: reversal zone, expect a bounce
signals.rules: Price within 0.3 ATR of H3 = sell zone (reversal), of L3 = buy zone. A close above H4 = breakout long; below L4 = breakdown short.

signals.name: VWAP Bands
signals.origin: Session VWAP +/- volume-weighted standard deviation; institutional benchmark (Brian Shannon, 'Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP', 2023)
signals.reason: 1.7 sigma below VWAP, inside the bands
signals.rules: Price more than 2 sigma above VWAP is stretched: fade it unless ADX > 25 (then ride the band). More than 2 sigma below: the mirror. Within 0.5 sigma = at fair value, no bias.

signals.name: Opening Gap
signals.origin: Gap statistics (Scott Andrews, 'Understanding Gaps', 2011): gap-and-go vs gap-fill
signals.reason: Gap down -0.32% holding below the open (gap-and-go)
signals.rules: Gap >= 0.3% vs the previous close. Gap up holding above the open = continuation; trading back below the open = fade toward the previous close (fill). Already filled = no edge. Mirror for gap downs.

signals.name: NR7 Narrow Range
signals.origin: Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout' (1990)
signals.rules: A bar with the narrowest range of the last 7 (NR7) precedes expansion. If the last bar was NR7: breakout pending, no direction. If the previous bar was NR7: a close above its high = long, below its low = short.

signals.name: Market Profile Value Area
signals.origin: J. Peter Steidlmayer, CBOT Market Profile (1984); volume-at-price of the previous session, 70% value area
signals.rules: Close above the value area high (VAH) = buyers accepting higher prices; below the value area low (VAL) = sellers in control; inside value = balance, lean by side of the point of control (POC).

signals.name: Williams Alligator
signals.origin: Bill Williams, 'Trading Chaos' (1995); SMMA 13/8/5 shifted 8/5/3
signals.reason: Alligator eating down: lips < teeth < jaw, price below (1.9 ATR mouth)
signals.rules: Lips above teeth above jaw with price above the lips = uptrend (long). The mirror = downtrend (short). Lines intertwined = the alligator sleeps: no trade.

signals.name: Linear Regression Trend
signals.origin: Ordinary least squares on log price (classic regression channel)
signals.rules: Fit a line through the last 60 log-closes. Positive, statistically significant slope = up; negative = down. R-squared measures how clean the trend is.

signals.name: Autoregressive AR(5)
signals.origin: Box-Jenkins time-series forecasting (AR component of ARIMA)
signals.rules: Regress each return on the previous 5 returns, then roll the forecast forward. Sign of the cumulative forecast gives direction; size relative to volatility gives confidence.

signals.name: Monte Carlo (GBM)
signals.origin: Black-Scholes-Merton style geometric Brownian motion simulation
signals.rules: Simulate thousands of price paths using historical drift (shrunk 50% toward zero) and volatility. P(final > spot) is the up-probability; the 10th/90th percentiles bound the expected range.

signals.name: Pattern Analog (kNN)
signals.origin: Analog / nearest-neighbour forecasting (Lorenz 1969; widely used pattern-matching approach)
signals.rules: Normalise the last 20 returns, find the 30 most similar historical windows (Euclidean distance) and measure what price did over the next `horizon` bars. Share of positive outcomes = P(up).

signals.name: Hurst Regime
signals.origin: H.E. Hurst (1951); Peters, 'Fractal Market Analysis' (1994)
signals.rules: H > 0.55 = persistent / trending market (weight trend-followers up). H < 0.45 = mean-reverting (weight oscillators up). ~0.5 = random walk.

signals.name: Golden / Death Cross
signals.origin: Classic institutional trend rule (SMA 50/200)
signals.reason: SMA50 below SMA200 by 5.6%; price below SMA50
signals.rules: Bullish when SMA50 > SMA200 and price above both; bearish when SMA50 < SMA200 and price below.

signals.name: EMA 9/21 Crossover
signals.origin: Common swing-trading fast/slow EMA system
signals.rules: Long when EMA9 crosses above EMA21; short when it crosses below. Fresher crosses score higher.

signals.name: MACD Crossover

signals.name: Money Flow Index

signals.reason: No notable pattern on the last bars
signals.rules: Detects Engulfing, Hammer / Hanging Man, Shooting Star, Morning / Evening Star, Three White Soldiers / Black Crows, Doji. Reversal patterns count more after an extended move.

signals.name: Pivot Points
signals.origin: Classic floor-trader pivots (CME pit tradition); previous session's H/L/C on intraday charts
signals.reason: Price at support S1 - bounce zone
signals.rules: Above the pivot = bullish bias, targets R1/R2; below = bearish, targets S1/S2. Price sitting at S1/R1 within 0.3 ATR is a bounce zone.

signals.name: Fibonacci Retracement
signals.origin: Classic Fibonacci pullback trading (Elliott / Gann tradition)
signals.reason: Down-swing intact, not at a fib level
signals.rules: In an up-swing, a pullback holding 38.2/50/61.8% is a buy zone; in a down-swing a bounce into those levels is a sell zone. Beyond 78.6% the swing is invalidated.

signals.name: Support / Resistance
signals.origin: Classic technical analysis (Edwards & Magee, 'Technical Analysis of Stock Trends', 1948)
signals.rules: Nearest swing-high resistance / swing-low support. A close through a level on the last bar = breakout; a hold within 0.5 ATR = bounce.

signals.name: Central Pivot Range (CPR)
signals.origin: Frank Ochoa, 'Secrets of a Pivot Boss' (2010); previous-session pivot, BC, TC
signals.rules: Close above the top central pivot (TC) = bullish bias; below the bottom central (BC) = bearish; inside the range = no bias. A narrow CPR (< 1/12 of the previous session's range) signals a trend day and strengthens the call.

signals.name: Camarilla Pivots
signals.origin: Nick Scott (1989); widely used by Indian intraday traders. H3/L3 reversal, H4/L4 breakout
signals.reason: At L3 1191.36: reversal zone, expect a bounce
signals.rules: Price within 0.3 ATR of H3 = sell zone (reversal), of L3 = buy zone. A close above H4 = breakout long; below L4 = breakdown short.

signals.name: VWAP Bands
signals.origin: Session VWAP +/- volume-weighted standard deviation; institutional benchmark (Brian Shannon, 'Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP', 2023)
signals.reason: 1.7 sigma below VWAP, inside the bands
signals.rules: Price more than 2 sigma above VWAP is stretched: fade it unless ADX > 25 (then ride the band). More than 2 sigma below: the mirror. Within 0.5 sigma = at fair value, no bias.

signals.name: Opening Gap
signals.origin: Gap statistics (Scott Andrews, 'Understanding Gaps', 2011): gap-and-go vs gap-fill
signals.reason: Gap down -0.32% holding below the open (gap-and-go)
signals.rules: Gap >= 0.3% vs the previous close. Gap up holding above the open = continuation; trading back below the open = fade toward the previous close (fill). Already filled = no edge. Mirror for gap downs.

signals.name: NR7 Narrow Range
signals.origin: Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout' (1990)
signals.rules: A bar with the narrowest range of the last 7 (NR7) precedes expansion. If the last bar was NR7: breakout pending, no direction. If the previous bar was NR7: a close above its high = long, below its low = short.

signals.name: Market Profile Value Area
signals.origin: J. Peter Steidlmayer, CBOT Market Profile (1984); volume-at-price of the previous session, 70% value area
signals.rules: Close above the value area high (VAH) = buyers accepting higher prices; below the value area low (VAL) = sellers in control; inside value = balance, lean by side of the point of control (POC).

signals.name: Williams Alligator
signals.origin: Bill Williams, 'Trading Chaos' (1995); SMMA 13/8/5 shifted 8/5/3
signals.reason: Alligator eating down: lips < teeth < jaw, price below (1.9 ATR mouth)
signals.rules: Lips above teeth above jaw with price above the lips = uptrend (long). The mirror = downtrend (short). Lines intertwined = the alligator sleeps: no trade.

signals.name: Linear Regression Trend
signals.origin: Ordinary least squares on log price (classic regression channel)
signals.reason: Slope -0.088%/bar, t-stat -5.3, R2 0.33; projected -0.88% in 10 bars
signals.rules: Fit a line through the last 60 log-closes. Positive, statistically significant slope = up; negative = down. R-squared measures how clean the trend is.

signals.name: Autoregressive AR(5)
signals.origin: Box-Jenkins time-series forecasting (AR component of ARIMA)
signals.rules: Regress each return on the previous 5 returns, then roll the forecast forward. Sign of the cumulative forecast gives direction; size relative to volatility gives confidence.

signals.name: Monte Carlo (GBM)
signals.origin: Black-Scholes-Merton style geometric Brownian motion simulation
signals.rules: Simulate thousands of price paths using historical drift (shrunk 50% toward zero) and volatility. P(final > spot) is the up-probability; the 10th/90th percentiles bound the expected range.

signals.name: Pattern Analog (kNN)
signals.origin: Analog / nearest-neighbour forecasting (Lorenz 1969; widely used pattern-matching approach)
signals.reason: 17 of 30 closest historical patterns went up; median move +0.56%
signals.rules: Normalise the last 20 returns, find the 30 most similar historical windows (Euclidean distance) and measure what price did over the next `horizon` bars. Share of positive outcomes = P(up).

signals.origin: H.E. Hurst (1951); Peters, 'Fractal Market Analysis' (1994)
signals.rules: H > 0.55 = persistent / trending market (weight trend-followers up). H < 0.45 = mean-reverting (weight oscillators up). ~0.5 = random walk.

signals.reason: Price at support S1 - bounce zone

signals.name: Support / Resistance
signals.origin: Classic technical analysis (Edwards & Magee, 'Technical Analysis of Stock Trends', 1948)
signals.rules: Nearest swing-high resistance / swing-low support. A close through a level on the last bar = breakout; a hold within 0.5 ATR = bounce.

signals.name: Central Pivot Range (CPR)
signals.origin: Frank Ochoa, 'Secrets of a Pivot Boss' (2010); previous-session pivot, BC, TC
signals.rules: Close above the top central pivot (TC) = bullish bias; below the bottom central (BC) = bearish; inside the range = no bias. A narrow CPR (< 1/12 of the previous session's range) signals a trend day and strengthens the call.

signals.name: Camarilla Pivots
signals.origin: Nick Scott (1989); widely used by Indian intraday traders. H3/L3 reversal, H4/L4 breakout
signals.reason: At L3 1191.36: reversal zone, expect a bounce
signals.rules: Price within 0.3 ATR of H3 = sell zone (reversal), of L3 = buy zone. A close above H4 = breakout long; below L4 = breakdown short.

signals.name: VWAP Bands
signals.origin: Session VWAP +/- volume-weighted standard deviation; institutional benchmark (Brian Shannon, 'Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP', 2023)
signals.reason: 1.7 sigma below VWAP, inside the bands
signals.rules: Price more than 2 sigma above VWAP is stretched: fade it unless ADX > 25 (then ride the band). More than 2 sigma below: the mirror. Within 0.5 sigma = at fair value, no bias.

signals.name: Opening Gap
signals.origin: Gap statistics (Scott Andrews, 'Understanding Gaps', 2011): gap-and-go vs gap-fill
signals.reason: Gap down -0.32% holding below the open (gap-and-go)
signals.rules: Gap >= 0.3% vs the previous close. Gap up holding above the open = continuation; trading back below the open = fade toward the previous close (fill). Already filled = no edge. Mirror for gap downs.

signals.name: NR7 Narrow Range
signals.origin: Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout' (1990)
signals.rules: A bar with the narrowest range of the last 7 (NR7) precedes expansion. If the last bar was NR7: breakout pending, no direction. If the previous bar was NR7: a close above its high = long, below its low = short.

signals.rules: Close above the value area high (VAH) = buyers accepting higher prices; below the value area low (VAL) = sellers in control; inside value = balance, lean by side of the point of control (POC).

signals.origin: Bill Williams, 'Trading Chaos' (1995); SMMA 13/8/5 shifted 8/5/3
signals.reason: Alligator eating down: lips < teeth < jaw, price below (1.9 ATR mouth)
signals.rules: Lips above teeth above jaw with price above the lips = uptrend (long). The mirror = downtrend (short). Lines intertwined = the alligator sleeps: no trade.

signals.name: Linear Regression Trend
signals.origin: Ordinary least squares on log price (classic regression channel)
signals.reason: Slope -0.088%/bar, t-stat -5.3, R2 0.33; projected -0.88% in 10 bars
signals.rules: Fit a line through the last 60 log-closes. Positive, statistically significant slope = up; negative = down. R-squared measures how clean the trend is.

signals.origin: Box-Jenkins time-series forecasting (AR component of ARIMA)
signals.rules: Regress each return on the previous 5 returns, then roll the forecast forward. Sign of the cumulative forecast gives direction; size relative to volatility gives confidence.

signals.name: Monte Carlo (GBM)
signals.origin: Black-Scholes-Merton style geometric Brownian motion simulation
signals.rules: Simulate thousands of price paths using historical drift (shrunk 50% toward zero) and volatility. P(final > spot) is the up-probability; the 10th/90th percentiles bound the expected range.

signals.name: Pattern Analog (kNN)
signals.origin: Analog / nearest-neighbour forecasting (Lorenz 1969; widely used pattern-matching approach)
signals.reason: 17 of 30 closest historical patterns went up; median move +0.56%
signals.rules: Normalise the last 20 returns, find the 30 most similar historical windows (Euclidean distance) and measure what price did over the next `horizon` bars. Share of positive outcomes = P(up).

signals.rules: H > 0.55 = persistent / trending market (weight trend-followers up). H < 0.45 = mean-reverting (weight oscillators up). ~0.5 = random walk.

signals.name: Pattern Analog (kNN)
signals.origin: Analog / nearest-neighbour forecasting (Lorenz 1969; widely used pattern-matching approach)
signals.reason: 17 of 30 closest historical patterns went up; median move +0.56%

signals.name: Supertrend
signals.origin: Olivier Seban; ATR(10) x 3

signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978), AF 0.02 step, 0.20 max
signals.rules: Dots below price = uptrend (long); dots above price = downtrend (short).

signals.rules: Above the pivot = bullish bias, targets R1/R2; below = bearish, targets S1/S2. Price sitting at S1/R1 within 0.3 ATR is a bounce zone.

signals.name: Fibonacci Retracement
signals.origin: Classic Fibonacci pullback trading (Elliott / Gann tradition)
signals.reason: Up-swing intact, not at a fib level
signals.rules: In an up-swing, a pullback holding 38.2/50/61.8% is a buy zone; in a down-swing a bounce into those levels is a sell zone. Beyond 78.6% the swing is invalidated.

signals.name: Support / Resistance
signals.origin: Classic technical analysis (Edwards & Magee, 'Technical Analysis of Stock Trends', 1948)
signals.rules: Nearest swing-high resistance / swing-low support. A close through a level on the last bar = breakout; a hold within 0.5 ATR = bounce.

signals.name: Central Pivot Range (CPR)
signals.origin: Frank Ochoa, 'Secrets of a Pivot Boss' (2010); previous-session pivot, BC, TC
signals.rules: Close above the top central pivot (TC) = bullish bias; below the bottom central (BC) = bearish; inside the range = no bias. A narrow CPR (< 1/12 of the previous session's range) signals a trend day and strengthens the call.

signals.name: Camarilla Pivots
signals.origin: Nick Scott (1989); widely used by Indian intraday traders. H3/L3 reversal, H4/L4 breakout
signals.reason: At H3 1542.68: reversal zone, expect a fade
signals.rules: Price within 0.3 ATR of H3 = sell zone (reversal), of L3 = buy zone. A close above H4 = breakout long; below L4 = breakdown short.

signals.name: VWAP Bands
signals.origin: Session VWAP +/- volume-weighted standard deviation; institutional benchmark (Brian Shannon, 'Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP', 2023)
signals.reason: 1.5 sigma above VWAP, inside the bands
signals.rules: Price more than 2 sigma above VWAP is stretched: fade it unless ADX > 25 (then ride the band). More than 2 sigma below: the mirror. Within 0.5 sigma = at fair value, no bias.

signals.name: Opening Gap
signals.origin: Gap statistics (Scott Andrews, 'Understanding Gaps', 2011): gap-and-go vs gap-fill
signals.rules: Gap >= 0.3% vs the previous close. Gap up holding above the open = continuation; trading back below the open = fade toward the previous close (fill). Already filled = no edge. Mirror for gap downs.

signals.name: NR7 Narrow Range
signals.origin: Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout' (1990)
signals.rules: A bar with the narrowest range of the last 7 (NR7) precedes expansion. If the last bar was NR7: breakout pending, no direction. If the previous bar was NR7: a close above its high = long, below its low = short.

signals.name: Market Profile Value Area
signals.origin: J. Peter Steidlmayer, CBOT Market Profile (1984); volume-at-price of the previous session, 70% value area
signals.rules: Close above the value area high (VAH) = buyers accepting higher prices; below the value area low (VAL) = sellers in control; inside value = balance, lean by side of the point of control (POC).

signals.name: Williams Alligator
signals.origin: Bill Williams, 'Trading Chaos' (1995); SMMA 13/8/5 shifted 8/5/3
signals.reason: Alligator eating up: lips > teeth > jaw, price above (1.7 ATR mouth)
signals.rules: Lips above teeth above jaw with price above the lips = uptrend (long). The mirror = downtrend (short). Lines intertwined = the alligator sleeps: no trade.

signals.name: Linear Regression Trend
signals.origin: Ordinary least squares on log price (classic regression channel)
signals.reason: Slope +0.064%/bar, t-stat 3.4, R2 0.17; projected +0.64% in 10 bars
signals.rules: Fit a line through the last 60 log-closes. Positive, statistically significant slope = up; negative = down. R-squared measures how clean the trend is.

signals.name: Autoregressive AR(5)
signals.origin: Box-Jenkins time-series forecasting (AR component of ARIMA)
signals.rules: Regress each return on the previous 5 returns, then roll the forecast forward. Sign of the cumulative forecast gives direction; size relative to volatility gives confidence.

signals.name: Monte Carlo (GBM)
signals.origin: Black-Scholes-Merton style geometric Brownian motion simulation
signals.rules: Simulate thousands of price paths using historical drift (shrunk 50% toward zero) and volatility. P(final > spot) is the up-probability; the 10th/90th percentiles bound the expected range.

signals.name: Pattern Analog (kNN)
signals.origin: Analog / nearest-neighbour forecasting (Lorenz 1969; widely used pattern-matching approach)
signals.reason: 16 of 30 closest historical patterns went up; median move +0.22%
signals.rules: Normalise the last 20 returns, find the 30 most similar historical windows (Euclidean distance) and measure what price did over the next `horizon` bars. Share of positive outcomes = P(up).

signals.name: Hurst Regime
signals.origin: H.E. Hurst (1951); Peters, 'Fractal Market Analysis' (1994)
signals.rules: H > 0.55 = persistent / trending market (weight trend-followers up). H < 0.45 = mean-reverting (weight oscillators up). ~0.5 = random walk.

signals.name: Golden / Death Cross
signals.origin: Classic institutional trend rule (SMA 50/200)
signals.reason: SMA50 above SMA200 by 8.3%; price above SMA50
signals.rules: Bullish when SMA50 > SMA200 and price above both; bearish when SMA50 < SMA200 and price below.

signals.name: EMA 9/21 Crossover
signals.origin: Common swing-trading fast/slow EMA system
signals.rules: Long when EMA9 crosses above EMA21; short when it crosses below. Fresher crosses score higher.

signals.name: MACD Crossover
signals.origin: Gerald Appel (1979), 12/26/9
signals.reason: MACD above signal; above zero line; histogram fading
signals.rules: Bullish: MACD above signal (esp. above zero) with rising histogram. Bearish: the reverse.

signals.name: ADX / DMI Trend
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978), 14-period
signals.reason: ADX 19.7 < 20: range-bound, no trend to follow
signals.rules: ADX > 25 = trending. +DI > -DI bullish, -DI > +DI bearish. ADX < 20 = no trend (neutral).

signals.name: Supertrend
signals.origin: Olivier Seban; ATR(10) x 3
signals.reason: Price above Supertrend (1452.51), 5.4% away - recent flip
signals.rules: Long while close is above the Supertrend line; short while below. Flips on close crossing the line.

signals.name: Parabolic SAR
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978), AF 0.02 step, 0.20 max
signals.rules: Dots below price = uptrend (long); dots above price = downtrend (short).

signals.name: Ichimoku Cloud
signals.origin: Goichi Hosoda (1960s), 9/26/52
signals.reason: price above cloud, Tenkan > Kijun, bearish (red) cloud, Chikou above price
signals.rules: Bullish: price above cloud, Tenkan > Kijun, green cloud (A > B). Bearish: the mirror. Inside cloud = neutral.

signals.name: Hull MA Slope
signals.origin: Alan Hull (2005), HMA 20
signals.rules: Long when HMA is rising and price above it; short when falling and price below.

signals.name: Elder Triple Screen
signals.origin: Dr. Alexander Elder, 'Trading for a Living' (1993)
signals.reason: Weekly-equivalent tide up (EMA13 rising, MACD-hist rising); Stoch 83
signals.rules: Screen 1: higher-timeframe trend via EMA13 slope & MACD histogram. Screen 2: buy pullbacks (Stoch < 30) in uptrend, sell rallies (Stoch > 70) in downtrend.

signals.name: Chandelier Exit
signals.origin: Chuck LeBeau; 22-period high/low, 3 x ATR(22)
signals.rules: Stay long while close > 22-bar high - 3 ATR; stay short while close < 22-bar low + 3 ATR.

signals.name: Heikin-Ashi Trend
signals.origin: Japanese 'average bar' charting; widely used trend filter
signals.rules: Consecutive same-colour HA candles = trend. No lower wick (bull) / no upper wick (bear) = strong.

signals.name: RSI 14 (Wilder)
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978)
signals.rules: RSI < 30 oversold (bullish reversal), > 70 overbought (bearish). Between: RSI > 50 bullish bias, < 50 bearish. Divergence strengthens the call.

signals.name: Connors RSI-2
signals.origin: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work' (2008)
signals.rules: Long: close > SMA200 and RSI(2) < 10 (extreme 5). Short: close < SMA200 and RSI(2) > 90. Exit when price crosses SMA5.

signals.name: Stochastic Oscillator
signals.origin: George Lane (1950s), 14/3/3
signals.rules: Bullish: %K crosses above %D below 20. Bearish: %K crosses below %D above 80. Mid-range crosses are weaker.

signals.name: CCI (Lambert)
signals.origin: Donald Lambert (1980), 20-period
signals.rules: Cross above +100 = bullish momentum; cross below -100 = bearish. Beyond +/-200 = exhaustion.

signals.name: Williams %R
signals.origin: Larry Williams, 14-period
signals.rules: Below -80 oversold (bullish), above -20 overbought (bearish).

signals.name: Academic Momentum (12-1)
signals.origin: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993); 60-bar lookback skipping last 5
signals.rules: Positive trailing return (excluding the most recent bars) predicts continuation; negative predicts further weakness.

signals.name: 52-Week High Momentum
signals.origin: George & Hwang, Journal of Finance (2004)
signals.rules: Price within ~5% of its 52-week high = bullish anchoring effect; near the 52-week low = bearish.

signals.name: Bollinger Squeeze Breakout
signals.origin: John Bollinger, 'Bollinger on Bollinger Bands' (2001); 20/2
signals.rules: BandWidth at multi-period low = squeeze. Close above upper band = bullish breakout; below lower = bearish. Walking the band continues the trend.

signals.name: Bollinger %B Mean Reversion
signals.origin: John Bollinger; classic range-trading application (with ADX < 25 filter)
signals.rules: In a non-trending market (ADX < 25), %B < 0 = buy back toward the middle band; %B > 1 = sell.

signals.name: TTM Squeeze
signals.origin: John Carter, 'Mastering the Trade' (2005); BB(20,2) inside KC(20,1.5)
signals.rules: Squeeze ON when Bollinger Bands sit inside Keltner Channels. When it releases, trade the direction of the momentum histogram (linear regression of price vs. midline).

signals.name: Turtle Breakout (Donchian)
signals.origin: Richard Dennis & William Eckhardt (1983); Donchian 20/55, exit 10
signals.rules: Buy a close above the prior 20-bar high (55-bar for System 2); sell a close below the prior 20-bar low. Exit on a 10-bar reverse breakout.

signals.name: Keltner Pullback
signals.origin: Chester Keltner / Linda Bradford Raschke; EMA20 +/- 1.5 ATR
signals.rules: Recent close above upper channel = uptrend; buy pullbacks to the midline. Recent close below lower = downtrend; sell rallies to midline.

signals.name: Volume-Confirmed Breakout
signals.origin: Stan Weinstein 'Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets' (1988); Stage analysis
signals.rules: A close beyond the prior 20-bar range on >= 1.5x 20-bar average volume is confirmed; breakouts on low volume are suspect.

signals.name: Opening Range Breakout
signals.origin: Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns' (1990)
signals.reason: Intraday strategy - not applicable on this timeframe
signals.rules: Intraday: the first 30 minutes define the range; a close above it is bullish, below it bearish for the session.

signals.name: On-Balance Volume
signals.origin: Joseph Granville (1963)
signals.reason: OBV above its EMA and rising: volume confirms uptrend
signals.rules: OBV above its 20-EMA and rising confirms an uptrend (volume flows in); OBV falling while price rises = bearish divergence.

signals.name: VWAP
signals.origin: Institutional execution benchmark; standard intraday bias tool
signals.rules: Price above VWAP = bullish bias (longs favoured, VWAP acts as support); below = bearish. Distance is normalised by ATR.

signals.name: Money Flow Index
signals.origin: Gene Quong & Avrum Soudack; 14-period

signals.name: Hull MA Slope

signals.rules: Stay long while close > 22-bar high - 3 ATR; stay short while close < 22-bar low + 3 ATR.

signals.origin: Japanese 'average bar' charting; widely used trend filter

signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978)
signals.rules: RSI < 30 oversold (bullish reversal), > 70 overbought (bearish). Between: RSI > 50 bullish bias, < 50 bearish. Divergence strengthens the call.

signals.name: Connors RSI-2
signals.origin: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work' (2008)
signals.rules: Long: close > SMA200 and RSI(2) < 10 (extreme 5). Short: close < SMA200 and RSI(2) > 90. Exit when price crosses SMA5.

signals.rules: Bullish: %K crosses above %D below 20. Bearish: %K crosses below %D above 80. Mid-range crosses are weaker.

signals.name: CCI (Lambert)
signals.origin: Donald Lambert (1980), 20-period
signals.rules: Cross above +100 = bullish momentum; cross below -100 = bearish. Beyond +/-200 = exhaustion.

signals.name: Williams %R
signals.origin: Larry Williams, 14-period
signals.rules: Below -80 oversold (bullish), above -20 overbought (bearish).

signals.name: Academic Momentum (12-1)

signals.rules: Positive trailing return (excluding the most recent bars) predicts continuation; negative predicts further weakness.

signals.name: 52-Week High Momentum
signals.origin: George & Hwang, Journal of Finance (2004)
signals.rules: Price within ~5% of its 52-week high = bullish anchoring effect; near the 52-week low = bearish.

signals.rules: BandWidth at multi-period low = squeeze. Close above upper band = bullish breakout; below lower = bearish. Walking the band continues the trend.

signals.origin: John Bollinger; classic range-trading application (with ADX < 25 filter)
signals.rules: In a non-trending market (ADX < 25), %B < 0 = buy back toward the middle band; %B > 1 = sell.

signals.rules: Squeeze ON when Bollinger Bands sit inside Keltner Channels. When it releases, trade the direction of the momentum histogram (linear regression of price vs. midline).

signals.origin: J. Peter Steidlmayer, CBOT Market Profile (1984); volume-at-price of the previous session, 70% value area
signals.rules: Close above the value area high (VAH) = buyers accepting higher prices; below the value area low (VAL) = sellers in control; inside value = balance, lean by side of the point of control (POC).

signals.name: Williams Alligator
signals.origin: Bill Williams, 'Trading Chaos' (1995); SMMA 13/8/5 shifted 8/5/3
signals.reason: Alligator eating up: lips > teeth > jaw, price above (1.7 ATR mouth)
signals.rules: Lips above teeth above jaw with price above the lips = uptrend (long). The mirror = downtrend (short). Lines intertwined = the alligator sleeps: no trade.

signals.name: Linear Regression Trend
signals.origin: Ordinary least squares on log price (classic regression channel)
signals.reason: Slope +0.064%/bar, t-stat 3.4, R2 0.17; projected +0.64% in 10 bars
signals.rules: Fit a line through the last 60 log-closes. Positive, statistically significant slope = up; negative = down. R-squared measures how clean the trend is.

signals.name: Autoregressive AR(5)
signals.origin: Box-Jenkins time-series forecasting (AR component of ARIMA)
signals.rules: Regress each return on the previous 5 returns, then roll the forecast forward. Sign of the cumulative forecast gives direction; size relative to volatility gives confidence.

signals.name: Monte Carlo (GBM)
signals.origin: Black-Scholes-Merton style geometric Brownian motion simulation
signals.rules: Simulate thousands of price paths using historical drift (shrunk 50% toward zero) and volatility. P(final > spot) is the up-probability; the 10th/90th percentiles bound the expected range.

signals.name: Pattern Analog (kNN)
signals.origin: Analog / nearest-neighbour forecasting (Lorenz 1969; widely used pattern-matching approach)
signals.reason: 16 of 30 closest historical patterns went up; median move +0.22%
signals.rules: Normalise the last 20 returns, find the 30 most similar historical windows (Euclidean distance) and measure what price did over the next `horizon` bars. Share of positive outcomes = P(up).

signals.name: Hurst Regime
signals.origin: H.E. Hurst (1951); Peters, 'Fractal Market Analysis' (1994)
signals.rules: H > 0.55 = persistent / trending market (weight trend-followers up). H < 0.45 = mean-reverting (weight oscillators up). ~0.5 = random walk.

signals.name: Golden / Death Cross
signals.origin: Classic institutional trend rule (SMA 50/200)
signals.reason: SMA50 above SMA200 by 8.3%; price above SMA50
signals.rules: Bullish when SMA50 > SMA200 and price above both; bearish when SMA50 < SMA200 and price below.

signals.name: EMA 9/21 Crossover
signals.origin: Common swing-trading fast/slow EMA system
signals.rules: Long when EMA9 crosses above EMA21; short when it crosses below. Fresher crosses score higher.

signals.name: MACD Crossover
signals.origin: Gerald Appel (1979), 12/26/9
signals.reason: MACD above signal; above zero line; histogram fading
signals.rules: Bullish: MACD above signal (esp. above zero) with rising histogram. Bearish: the reverse.

signals.name: ADX / DMI Trend
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978), 14-period
signals.reason: ADX 19.7 < 20: range-bound, no trend to follow
signals.rules: ADX > 25 = trending. +DI > -DI bullish, -DI > +DI bearish. ADX < 20 = no trend (neutral).

signals.name: Supertrend
signals.origin: Olivier Seban; ATR(10) x 3
signals.reason: Price above Supertrend (1452.51), 5.4% away - recent flip
signals.rules: Long while close is above the Supertrend line; short while below. Flips on close crossing the line.

signals.name: Parabolic SAR
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978), AF 0.02 step, 0.20 max
signals.rules: Dots below price = uptrend (long); dots above price = downtrend (short).

signals.name: Ichimoku Cloud
signals.origin: Goichi Hosoda (1960s), 9/26/52
signals.reason: price above cloud, Tenkan > Kijun, bearish (red) cloud, Chikou above price
signals.rules: Bullish: price above cloud, Tenkan > Kijun, green cloud (A > B). Bearish: the mirror. Inside cloud = neutral.

signals.name: Hull MA Slope
signals.origin: Alan Hull (2005), HMA 20
signals.rules: Long when HMA is rising and price above it; short when falling and price below.

signals.name: Elder Triple Screen
signals.origin: Dr. Alexander Elder, 'Trading for a Living' (1993)
signals.reason: Weekly-equivalent tide up (EMA13 rising, MACD-hist rising); Stoch 83
signals.rules: Screen 1: higher-timeframe trend via EMA13 slope & MACD histogram. Screen 2: buy pullbacks (Stoch < 30) in uptrend, sell rallies (Stoch > 70) in downtrend.

signals.name: Chandelier Exit
signals.origin: Chuck LeBeau; 22-period high/low, 3 x ATR(22)
signals.rules: Stay long while close > 22-bar high - 3 ATR; stay short while close < 22-bar low + 3 ATR.

signals.name: Heikin-Ashi Trend
signals.origin: Japanese 'average bar' charting; widely used trend filter
signals.rules: Consecutive same-colour HA candles = trend. No lower wick (bull) / no upper wick (bear) = strong.

signals.name: RSI 14 (Wilder)
signals.origin: J. Welles Wilder (1978)
signals.rules: RSI < 30 oversold (bullish reversal), > 70 overbought (bearish). Between: RSI > 50 bullish bias, < 50 bearish. Divergence strengthens the call.

signals.name: Connors RSI-2
signals.origin: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work' (2008)
signals.rules: Long: close > SMA200 and RSI(2) < 10 (extreme 5). Short: close < SMA200 and RSI(2) > 90. Exit when price crosses SMA5.

signals.name: Stochastic Oscillator
signals.origin: George Lane (1950s), 14/3/3
signals.rules: Bullish: %K crosses above %D below 20. Bearish: %K crosses below %D above 80. Mid-range crosses are weaker.

signals.name: CCI (Lambert)
signals.origin: Donald Lambert (1980), 20-period
signals.rules: Cross above +100 = bullish momentum; cross below -100 = bearish. Beyond +/-200 = exhaustion.

signals.name: Williams %R
signals.origin: Larry Williams, 14-period
signals.rules: Below -80 oversold (bullish), above -20 overbought (bearish).

signals.name: Academic Momentum (12-1)
signals.origin: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993); 60-bar lookback skipping last 5
signals.rules: Positive trailing return (excluding the most recent bars) predicts continuation; negative predicts further weakness.

signals.name: 52-Week High Momentum
signals.origin: George & Hwang, Journal of Finance (2004)
signals.rules: Price within ~5% of its 52-week high = bullish anchoring effect; near the 52-week low = bearish.

signals.name: Bollinger Squeeze Breakout
signals.origin: John Bollinger, 'Bollinger on Bollinger Bands' (2001); 20/2
signals.rules: BandWidth at multi-period low = squeeze. Close above upper band = bullish breakout; below lower = bearish. Walking the band continues the trend.

signals.name: Bollinger %B Mean Reversion
signals.origin: John Bollinger; classic range-trading application (with ADX < 25 filter)
signals.rules: In a non-trending market (ADX < 25), %B < 0 = buy back toward the middle band; %B > 1 = sell.

signals.name: TTM Squeeze
signals.origin: John Carter, 'Mastering the Trade' (2005); BB(20,2) inside KC(20,1.5)
signals.rules: Squeeze ON when Bollinger Bands sit inside Keltner Channels. When it releases, trade the direction of the momentum histogram (linear regression of price vs. midline).

signals.name: Turtle Breakout (Donchian)
signals.origin: Richard Dennis & William Eckhardt (1983); Donchian 20/55, exit 10
signals.rules: Buy a close above the prior 20-bar high (55-bar for System 2); sell a close below the prior 20-bar low. Exit on a 10-bar reverse breakout.

signals.name: Keltner Pullback
signals.origin: Chester Keltner / Linda Bradford Raschke; EMA20 +/- 1.5 ATR
signals.rules: Recent close above upper channel = uptrend; buy pullbacks to the midline. Recent close below lower = downtrend; sell rallies to midline.

signals.name: Volume-Confirmed Breakout
signals.origin: Stan Weinstein 'Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets' (1988); Stage analysis
signals.rules: A close beyond the prior 20-bar range on >= 1.5x 20-bar average volume is confirmed; breakouts on low volume are suspect.

signals.name: Opening Range Breakout
signals.origin: Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns' (1990)
signals.reason: Intraday strategy - not applicable on this timeframe
signals.rules: Intraday: the first 30 minutes define the range; a close above it is bullish, below it bearish for the session.

signals.name: On-Balance Volume
signals.origin: Joseph Granville (1963)
signals.reason: OBV above its EMA and rising: volume confirms uptrend
signals.rules: OBV above its 20-EMA and rising confirms an uptrend (volume flows in); OBV falling while price rises = bearish divergence.

signals.name: VWAP
signals.origin: Institutional execution benchmark; standard intraday bias tool
signals.rules: Price above VWAP = bullish bias (longs favoured, VWAP acts as support); below = bearish. Distance is normalised by ATR.

signals.name: Money Flow Index
signals.origin: Gene Quong & Avrum Soudack; 14-period
signals.rules: MFI < 20 oversold (bullish), > 80 overbought (bearish).

signals.name: Chaikin Money Flow
signals.origin: Marc Chaikin; 20-period
signals.rules: CMF > +0.05 = buying pressure (bullish); < -0.05 = selling pressure (bearish).

signals.name: Candlestick Patterns
signals.origin: Steve Nison, 'Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques' (1991)
signals.reason: No notable pattern on the last bars
signals.rules: Detects Engulfing, Hammer / Hanging Man, Shooting Star, Morning / Evening Star, Three White Soldiers / Black Crows, Doji. Reversal patterns count more after an extended move.

signals.name: Pivot Points
signals.origin: Classic floor-trader pivots (CME pit tradition); previous session's H/L/C on intraday charts
signals.rules: Above the pivot = bullish bias, targets R1/R2; below = bearish, targets S1/S2. Price sitting at S1/R1 within 0.3 ATR is a bounce zone.

signals.name: Fibonacci Retracement
signals.origin: Classic Fibonacci pullback trading (Elliott / Gann tradition)
signals.reason: Up-swing intact, not at a fib level
signals.rules: In an up-swing, a pullback holding 38.2/50/61.8% is a buy zone; in a down-swing a bounce into those levels is a sell zone. Beyond 78.6% the swing is invalidated.

signals.name: Support / Resistance
signals.origin: Classic technical analysis (Edwards & Magee, 'Technical Analysis of Stock Trends', 1948)
signals.rules: Nearest swing-high resistance / swing-low support. A close through a level on the last bar = breakout; a hold within 0.5 ATR = bounce.

signals.name: Central Pivot Range (CPR)
signals.origin: Frank Ochoa, 'Secrets of a Pivot Boss' (2010); previous-session pivot, BC, TC
signals.rules: Close above the top central pivot (TC) = bullish bias; below the bottom central (BC) = bearish; inside the range = no bias. A narrow CPR (< 1/12 of the previous session's range) signals a trend day and strengthens the call.

signals.name: Camarilla Pivots
signals.origin: Nick Scott (1989); widely used by Indian intraday traders. H3/L3 reversal, H4/L4 breakout
signals.reason: At H3 1542.68: reversal zone, expect a fade
signals.rules: Price within 0.3 ATR of H3 = sell zone (reversal), of L3 = buy zone. A close above H4 = breakout long; below L4 = breakdown short.

signals.name: VWAP Bands
signals.origin: Session VWAP +/- volume-weighted standard deviation; institutional benchmark (Brian Shannon, 'Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP', 2023)
signals.reason: 1.5 sigma above VWAP, inside the bands
signals.rules: Price more than 2 sigma above VWAP is stretched: fade it unless ADX > 25 (then ride the band). More than 2 sigma below: the mirror. Within 0.5 sigma = at fair value, no bias.

signals.name: Opening Gap
signals.origin: Gap statistics (Scott Andrews, 'Understanding Gaps', 2011): gap-and-go vs gap-fill
signals.rules: Gap >= 0.3% vs the previous close. Gap up holding above the open = continuation; trading back below the open = fade toward the previous close (fill). Already filled = no edge. Mirror for gap downs.

signals.name: NR7 Narrow Range
signals.origin: Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout' (1990)
signals.rules: A bar with the narrowest range of the last 7 (NR7) precedes expansion. If the last bar was NR7: breakout pending, no direction. If the previous bar was NR7: a close above its high = long, below its low = short.

catalog.doc: SMA50 / SMA200 Golden Cross & Death Cross - the classic long-term trend filter.
EMA 9/21 crossover - the standard swing / day-trading fast trend signal.
Gerald Appel's MACD (12,26,9): signal-line cross + zero-line + histogram momentum.
Wilder's ADX / DMI: trade in the direction of DI dominance only when ADX shows a trend (>20-25).
Supertrend (10, 3) - ATR-based trailing trend indicator popular with Indian intraday traders.
Wilder's Parabolic SAR (0.02, 0.2) stop-and-reverse.
Ichimoku Kinko Hyo: price vs Kumo cloud, Tenkan/Kijun cross, cloud colour.
Alan Hull's HMA(20) slope - a low-lag trend direction filter.

Alexander Elder's Triple Screen: higher-timeframe tide (EMA13 slope / MACD-hist on 5x bars),
then trade pullbacks on the base timeframe oscillator (Stochastic / Force Index).
Chuck LeBeau's Chandelier Exit: 22-bar high - 3 x ATR(22) (long) / 22-bar low + 3 x ATR (short).
Heikin-Ashi candle colour run; candles with no wick against the trend = strong trend.
Wilder's RSI(14): 30/70 reversal zones, 50 midline as trend bias, plus simple divergence check.
Larry Connors' RSI(2) mean-reversion: buy RSI2 < 10 above SMA200, sell RSI2 > 90 below SMA200. Exit at SMA5.
George Lane's Stochastic (14,3,3): %K/%D crosses in the 20/80 zones.
Donald Lambert's CCI(20): +100/-100 breakout rules (trend) and extremes (reversal).
Larry Williams' %R(14): -20 / -80 zones.

Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) cross-sectional momentum, adapted to a single asset:
return over the past 12 'months' skipping the most recent 1 (uses 60-bar / 5-bar analog).
George & Hwang (2004): nearness to the 52-week high predicts future returns.
John Bollinger's Squeeze: BandWidth at a 120-bar low then a close outside the bands starts a move.
Bollinger %B mean reversion when ADX shows no trend.
John Carter's TTM Squeeze: Bollinger inside Keltner = squeeze on; fire in the momentum direction on release.

Turtle Trading (Richard Dennis & William Eckhardt, 1983): System 1 = 20-day Donchian breakout,
System 2 = 55-day breakout. Exit on 10-day opposite breakout.
Linda Raschke's Keltner Channel trend-pullback: trend by channel breakouts, enter on pullbacks to the EMA20 midline.
Stan Weinstein / classic breakout confirmation: a range break on >= 1.5x average volume.
Toby Crabel's Opening Range Breakout (intraday only): break of the first 30 minutes' range.
Joseph Granville's On-Balance Volume: OBV trend confirms price; divergence warns.
Institutional VWAP: price above VWAP = buyers in control (session VWAP intraday, 20-bar rolling otherwise).
Money Flow Index (volume-weighted RSI): 20/80 zones.
Marc Chaikin's CMF(20): sustained > +0.05 accumulation, < -0.05 distribution.
Japanese candlestick reversal patterns as catalogued by Steve Nison.
Classic floor-trader pivot points (P, R1-3, S1-3) from the previous session (intraday) or previous bar.
Fibonacci retracement of the last major swing: 38.2 / 50 / 61.8 pullbacks in the swing direction.
Swing-point support / resistance: reaction at the nearest level, or a clean break.

Frank Ochoa's Central Pivot Range: previous-session pivot / BC / TC; price above the range is bullish,
below bearish; a narrow CPR marks a likely trend day.
Camarilla pivots: fade the H3 / L3 reversal zone, follow a break of H4 / L4.
Session VWAP with volume-weighted standard-deviation bands: stretched beyond 2 sigma reverts unless the trend is strong.
Gap trading: a gap that holds beyond the open tends to continue (gap-and-go); one that trades back through the open tends to fill.
Toby Crabel's NR7: the narrowest range in seven bars precedes a range expansion; trade the break of that bar.
Market Profile value area: acceptance above the value area high is bullish, below the value area low bearish.
Bill Williams' Alligator: lips > teeth > jaw with price above = eating up (trend); intertwined = sleeping.
